title: Taking Over a New House in 2027: What to Check Before the Final Payment
desc: Handover checklist for a newly built house: check structure, waterproofing, utilities, doors, as-built records and warranty before making the final payment.
summary: A list of items owners should inspect themselves and the records to receive when taking over a newly built house, before making the final payment and retaining the warranty money.
body: p

The final payment is the owner's last lever for getting the contractor to fix remaining defects. Under the law, a building may be put into use only after acceptance confirms it meets the design and standards (Clause 2, Article 57 of the Construction Law 2025). The acceptance procedure is covered in Acceptance of residential buildings; this article focuses on the physical inspection when you take over the house.
h2
1. Preparing before the handover
ul
Bring the design drawings, the materials schedule from the contract, a tape measure, a spirit level or long straightedge, a torch and a marker.
Inspect in daylight; if possible, inspect again after a rainstorm to see where water gets in.
Bring a qualified person if the house is large or you have not hired a supervisor.
h2
2. Structure, walls and floors
ul

Look at the beams, slabs and columns for cracks, sagging, exposed reinforcement and honeycombing. Hairline cracks in the plaster layer differ from cracks running through the structure – abnormal, long or spreading cracks must be assessed by an engineer.
Walls: flat, straight, with no blistering; tap the plaster and tiling to listen for hollow sounds.
Tiled floors: flatness, even grout lines, no warped edges; bathroom and balcony floors must slope correctly toward drainage.
h2
3. Waterproofing and drainage
ul
Flood-test the bathroom floors, roof terrace and balcony (if the contractor has not done so with a record), then check the ceiling of the floor below.
Check gutters, roof drain pipes and the joint with the neighbouring house; check whether the ground-floor wall bases are damp or mouldy.
Open all taps and flush simultaneously on several floors to see whether drainage is quick and whether any bad smell comes back up.
h2
4. Electricity, water, doors and fittings
ul
Test each switch, socket (with a voltage tester) and light; check that the distribution board has shock-protection devices and labels each circuit.
Check water pressure and look for leaks under sinks, toilets, water heaters and pumps.
Open and close every door and lock; doors must not scrape the floor, glass must not be cracked, and seals must be tight.
Compare the items installed (tiles, paint, sanitary ware, electrical cable) with the signed materials schedule.
h2
5. Records you must receive
p

Before handover, the construction contractor must give the investor the as-built drawings, operating instructions, maintenance procedures, equipment list, spare materials and supplies and related documents (Clause 3, Article 58 of the Construction Law; Clause 2, Article 30 of Decree 207/2026). Record the handover in a written minute listing the remaining defects and the deadline to fix them. Preparing the as-built drawings is the contractor's obligation (Point h, Clause 2, Article 61); failing to prepare them can be fined VND 40–60 million for an organisation (Point a, Clause 3, Article 23 of Decree 339/2026). The as-built drawings are needed when registering the house – see As-built completion and registering the house on the land use right certificate.
h2
6. Final payment and retaining the warranty money
ul
Pay only when the defects in the minute have been fixed, or hold back the corresponding amount.

The parties agree in the contract on the time, amount and form of the warranty security; if the contractor does not carry out warranty work, the owner may use this sum to hire someone else to fix it (Clause 2, Article 20 of Decree 210/2026). A private house has a minimum warranty of 24 months (Clause 2, Article 129 of the Housing Law) – see Warranty for houses.
Keep all records; records for managing and using the building must be kept for at least the building's service life (Clause 2, Article 42 of the Construction Law).
p
If you need someone to inspect with you when you take over the house, contact Quan Construction.
note

This article is for reference; every building needs to be surveyed and designed by qualified professionals. Cracks and structural sagging must be assessed by an engineer. Fines under Decree 339/2026/ND-CP are those for organisations; for individuals the amount is half. The Housing Law 2023 is partially no longer in force.
